Aristidis of Thebes II (b. 400 BCE, Thebes) was a musician or composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Thebes. Known for his work in the fields of painters and sculptors, Aristidis was part of a thriving artistic community that produced works of enduring beauty and significance. His compositions, though lost to time, would have been performed by skilled musicians in the theaters and temples of Thebes.

As a musician and composer, Aristidis of Thebes II was influenced by the cultural and artistic developments of his time, including the rise of Athens and the expansion of the Persian Empire. His work likely reflected the values of the Theban aristocracy, which placed a high premium on the arts and the pursuit of excellence.

Aristidis' legacy can be seen in the many surviving works of art from Thebes, including sculptures and paintings that demonstrate the skill and craftsmanship of the ancient Greeks. His compositions, though lost, would have contributed to the rich musical heritage of the Classical era, influencing generations of musicians and composers to come.

The fact that Aristidis of Thebes II is known from only a few scattered references speaks to the often fragmentary nature of historical records from ancient times. Nonetheless, his significance as a musician and composer is undeniable, and his work continues to inspire and delight audiences to this day.

In 360 BCE, Aristidis of Thebes II died, leaving behind a legacy of artistic excellence and cultural significance that continues to be felt in the world of music and art today.
